name: South Gate City Council
minutes_text:
CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  APRIL  8, 2025

CALLTO  ORDER  Joshua Barron,  Vice Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to
  order at 6:52 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina Fierro,  Deputy  Director  of Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Manuel  Arana,  Police  Captain

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Vice Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria  del Pilar Avalos,
  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  AI Rios;  City
  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City Attorney  Raul
  F. Salinas

ABSENT/EXCUSED  Mayor  Maria  Davila

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  - NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  Mario  Dominguez,  South  Gate resident,  concerned  that the Wi-Fi  in the
  Council  Chambers  keeps failing.  Mr. Dominguez  is not happy  with  the
  new design  for the ELAC  presentation.

  Students  on a group  assignment  for USC provided  pictures  of Frontage
  Road which  needs a lot of repair  work.  The fencing  that divides  the street
  and the 710 freeway  has been torn and ripped,  which  is dangerous  for the
  homeless  population.  Also,  trucks  and truckers  dump  trash.

  Roberto  Rodriguez,  South  Gate resident,  informed  the Council  that the
  residents  were not informed  of the increase  in trash services.

F.MAILS  Jennifer  Daily,  urging  the Council  to hold the Planning  Commission's
  unanimous  decision  on March  18, 2025, to reject  Engle's  appeal  for
  continued  metal  processing  operations  and zone change  at 8530 Alameda.

  Roberto  Sanchez  expresses  his frustration  with  how the city handles
  community  participation,  particularly  with  emails  and call-in  features  for
  the Council  meetings.  He accuses Council  Members  and City  staff using
  these tactics  to sensor participation.  He criticizes  the state of Tweedy
  Boulevard  and the library  as hazardous  due to crime.

  Maria  Chavez  expresses  frustration  with  city management  citing  several
  issues regarding  financial  mismanagement.  She criticizes  the proposed
  Utility  User Tax as a bailout  for the City  Council  and city  staff.  She
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF APRIL  8, 2025

EMAILS  CONT'D  regards  the Tweedy  Mile  Business  District  ongoing  repairs  as slopy  and
  poorly  executed.  She questions  the additional  taxpayer  monies  spent on
  Urban  Orchard  Park due to inadequate  planning.  She highlights  design
  flaws  on the Long  Beach  Boulevard  improvements  regarding  dangerous
  rocks placed  on the sidewalks  and then later removed.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works  stated receiving  questions  on
  Frontage  Road,  as well  as emails  to be addressed.  Mr. Cervantes  stated
  that the city takes pride  in maintaining  its roadways.  The challenges  are
  simply  funds.  Mr. Cervantes  stated Frontage  Road is scheduled  for repair.
  Public  Works  has completed  the designs.  Mr. Cervantes  stated the designs
  for Tweedy  are to meet safety  and ADA  standards.  The city did run into a
  procedural  and regulatory  issue on the Urban  Orchard  Project  with  LA
  accounting.  The Urban  Orchard  Project  is not being  funded  through  the
  general  fund but through  grants.  Regarding  the rocks  designed  on Long
  Beach  Boulevard,  the use of those rocks  or stones is industry  standard  and
  many  cities  are being  used. The design  was for places  where  the public
  does not walk  in, but the city understands  the potential  for safety  issues, so
  the design  is being  replaced  with  another  design.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked Mr. Cervantes  to speak about the increase  in the
  trash.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated that the city has a franchise  agreement  with  UWS  to
  provide solid waste and part of that there is an annual rate increase. The
  community  is notified by UWS, not by the city. He doesn't understand
  why  certain  individuals  don't  get to see them.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked if trucks  are allowed  to park on Frontage  Road
  adjacent  to the 710 freeway.

  Manuel  Arana,  Police  Captain,  believes  the city does not allow  trucks  to
  park on the street. The police  department  have had meetings  with
  businesses  owners  that allow  truck  drivers  to park on the street.

  Tina Fierro,  Deputy  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  mentioned  a couple
  of events  scheduled  for this weekend.

  David  Crabtree,  Interim  Director  of Community  Development  - nothing
  to report.

  StevenAragon,  Acting  Budget  and Finance  Manager  - nothing  to report.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources  - nothing  to report.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Manuel  Arana,  Police  Captain,  stated the topic  about homelessness  at the
  library  is a complex  topic  because the library  is a county  facility.  The
  reason the homeless  are at the library  is because  of the wi-fi  open to the
  public.  The captain  made it clear that being  homeless  is not a crime,
  however  due to the school  being close the police  department  have
  contacted  these individuals  to provide  resources.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager,  made a general  comment  on the
  community's  concerns.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  asked the City  Manager  to verify  why the city's
  website  was not working  to report  a pothole.  He also asked City  Manager
  to speak on the length  of time approved  by Council  to work  on the Tweedy
  Boulevard.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager,  will  verify  the city's  website.  He also spoke
  on the Tweedy  Boulevard  project.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney,  stated that the Public  Records  Brown  Act
  allows  for the surnmarization  of emails.

  Council  Member  Avalos  stated attending  a meeting  with  the Southeast
  Water  Coalition  last Thursday.  Three  important  issues were discussed
  regarding  WRD's  practices.  WRD  is scheduled  to have a public  hearing
  meeting  on April  29'h at 10:00 a.m. to discuss water rate increase.

  Council  Member  Avalos  will  also be attending  the Greater  Los Angeles
  Vector  Control  District  meeting  tomorrow.  Vector  Control  are also seeking
  to increase  their  rates. Vector  Control  are scheduled  to make a presentation
  at the May  13th City Council  meeting.  She thanked  City  Manager  for the
  South  Gate app. She encourages  the community  to use it. She cornrnended
  the Public  Works  Department  for fixing  a light  pole that had its wire
  pulled  out.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  stated that the International  Studies
  Learning  Center,  high  school  robotics  team has made it to the Robotics
  World  Championship  in Houston,  TX next week.  He mentioned  that if the
  team wins the World  Championship  it gives them an opportunity  to
  compete  globally  against  other countries.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  wishes  the team well  and whether  they win  or not they
  should  attend  a council  meeting  to be honored.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk  - nothing  to report.

REPORTS  AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated receiving  a lot of complaints  from
CONT'D

  residents  that city  employees  are taking  too long to come out when it has
  to do with  loud music,  vehicles  parked  on lawn, people working  as

  mechanics  on their  properties.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  mentioned  that the general  fund was not used

  for the Urban  Orchard  Project.  He would  like for the residents  to reach out

  to Council  and discuss  mismanage  of city funds.  He thanked  Mr. Crabtree

  for his time  as Interim  Director  of Community  Development.

  Council  Member  Rios asked if the city participated  in the Homeless
  Count.  Mentioned  that at the last City Council meeting the LACCD  had a

  presentation.  He walked  Tsveedy Boulevard  and made some observations.
  He inquired  if the prices  for the activities  at the park for the children be
  reduced.

  Vice  Mayor  spoke about mismanagement
  Barron  of funds. He stated that
  the Finance Department  has been awarded  three times  in a row an

  accountant  reward. He mentioned  that the budget hearings are held every
  year, and no one attends the meetings.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  attended  a meeting  with  the other eighty-eight  (88)

  Mayors  of LA  County  hosted  by Mayor  Karen Bass regarding  amazing

  events in LA County coming soon, including  FIFA  World  Cup in 2026,

  Super Bowl in 2027 and the Olympics  in 2028.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  supports  ELAC  being  in this community

EXCUSF,D  FROM

  At this time,  7:47 p.m.,  Council  Member  Avalos,  was excused  from  the
MEETING

  meeting  and departed  from  the Council  Chambers.
